By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.20<Z<2.10) & =P(Z<2.10)-P(Z\le -2.20) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.10)-P(Z\le -2.20) \\  & =Φ(2.10)-Φ(-2.20)\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-2.20) & =0.0139, \\ Φ(-2.10) & =0.0179,\end{aligned}
$$

but we are not given $Φ(2.10).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.10) & =P(Z\le 2.10) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -2.10) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.10) \\  & =1-0.0179 \\  & =0.9821\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.20<Z<2.10) & =Φ(2.10)-Φ(-2.20) \\  & =0.9821-0.0139 \\  & =0.9682.\end{aligned}
